findings.title: Same-integration suppression is overbroad for groups linked to multiple external issues
findings.body: should_sync now returns False whenever the assignment source's integration_id matches the target organization integration. AssignmentSource only carries integration_id, not the specific external issue that triggered the inbound change. sync_assignee_outbound uses the same assignment_source_dict for every GroupLink for the group, so if a group is linked to multiple external issues in the same integration, an inbound assignment from one of those issues suppresses outbound sync to all of them. The other linked issues in that integration will remain on the old assignee. The source should include the originating external issue key and the check should suppress only that external issue, or otherwise avoid suppressing unrelated linked issues.

findings.title: should_sync is now called with an extra argument that existing overrides may not accept
findings.body: The task now calls installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source). Previously should_sync was defined and overridden as should_sync(self, attribute). Any integration subclass that still overrides should_sync with the old single-argument signature will raise TypeError when outbound assignee sync runs, causing the task to fail and retry for that integration. All overrides must be updated or the task must call this without a second positional argument unless it knows the installation can accept it.

findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued uses import-time default instead of creation time
findings.body: queued: datetime = timezone.now() is evaluated once when the module is imported. Every AssignmentSource constructed without an explicit queued argument, including from_integration, therefore gets the module import time rather than the time the source was created. If queued is intended to track when the assignment source was queued or generated, use field(default_factory=timezone.now) from dataclasses so each instance is stamped at construction time.

findings.title: No regression test for same-source deassign suppression
findings.body: There is a test for assign with a matching source integration, but the inbound deassign path also passes AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration) in sync_group_assignee_inbound and should be suppressed by the same should_sync check. A Jira unassign webhook would still echo back to Jira if this path regresses or fails to propagate the source. Add a test where GroupAssignee.objects.deassign is called with a matching AssignmentSource and assert sync_assignee_outbound is not called.
